text.p: Following are the leading stories in Pakistani newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The caretaker federal and provincial governments have decided to cut drastically development and non-development expenses to bring down the budget deficit.

- Ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto has demanded that President Farooq Leghari should not sign any fresh agreement with the International Monetary Fund without taking the major political parties into confidence.

- The corps commanders of the Pakistani army discussed the internal and external security situation on Sunday and decided to extend all possible support, if requested, to hold free and fair elections on February 3.
- The Supreme Court of Pakistan entertained the "modified" petition of the ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto challenging the dissolution of the National Assembly and the ouster of her government.
- The government has decided to lift a ban on the use of cellular phones in Karachi but has asked service operators not to press for damages claims running into billion of rupees, sources said.
- The caretaker Minister for Petroleum has taken serious notice of the fact that the Saindak gold and copper project has remained in abeyance since last July for want of working capital.
- The Shell Group of Companies is contemplating a proposal to invest heavily in deep well explorations and to drill the first exploratory well in the Sor Range in northern Pakistan.
- The caretaker government is likely to announce a relief package for cooking oil manufacturers in the next few days to bring down prices of the commodity in the domestic markets.
- The European Union has approved import of Pakistani fine quality basmati rice, subject to certification of best quality.

- A high level British trade delegation led by Malcolm Sewell arrived on a six-day visit to Pakistan. The mission comprises representatives of 10 companies supplying a wide range of products to Pakistan.
